title: Cattan, Rodrigues & Congedo 2019 — Passive Head-Mounted Display Music-Listening EEG dataset (PHMD)
description: This dataset comprises electroencephalographic recordings from 12 healthy subjects during music listening with and without a passive head-mounted display (PHMD). A passive head-mounted display is a head-mounted device that includes no integrated electronics except for a smartphone. The study employed a resting-state paradigm with 16-channel EEG acquisition at 512 Hz, comparing neural activity across alternating blocks of smartphone-on and smartphone-off conditions during continuous music listening (Bach Invention compositions). The dataset provides raw, unfiltered EEG data in mat and csv formats, enabling investigation of how passive head-mounted displays and auditory stimuli influence brain electrical activity.
methods_description: EEG data were acquired from 12 subjects using a 16-channel g.USBamp system (sampling rate: 512 Hz) with wet electrodes in a standard 10-20 montage. Subjects sat approximately 50 cm from a screen and listened to Bach Invention compositions while focusing on a visual fixation marker. Each experimental session consisted of 10 blocks (60 seconds each) with randomized smartphone on/off conditions (5 blocks each). Data were recorded with no digital filtering and without a Faraday cage to simulate real-world conditions. Reference electrode was placed at the right earlobe with ground at AFz.
